newsitem.title: JAPAN: Angry investor wields knife at Nomura office.
newsitem.headline: Angry investor wields knife at Nomura office.

text.p: A disgruntled investor brandished a knife at a regional branch of Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Monday, demanding the scandal-tainted brokerage compensate for his investment trust portfolio losses, police said.

Tadao Nakano, 67, was promptly arrested and no one was hurt at the Nomura office in the central city of Nagoya in the latest outburst of anger at a massive illegal payoff scandal at Japan's largest securities house.
"I lost money in investment trusts. Give my money back," Nakano was quoted as yelling as he was arrested.
Nomura's business has suffered and the company faces the possibility that it may be ordered to suspend its business for up to six months for its links to a racketeer who is under arrest.

Ten arrests have already been made in the scandal, including Nomura's former president Hideo Sakamaki, three other Nomura executives and four officials at Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), Japan's second-largest bank in terms of deposits.
